name: 1 & 2 Kings

objectives.text: Identify Solomon as the king who asked God for wisdom and built the Temple in Jerusalem
Retell how God provided food for Elijah through the ravens and the widow of Zarephath
Describe how Elijah was taken up to heaven and how Elisha carried on his work as prophet
Recall that after Solomon the kingdom split into Israel in the north and Judah in the south
Summarize the contest between Elijah and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel
Retell the healing of Naaman and explain what it shows about God's power reaching beyond Israel
Explain how Solomon's sin and Rehoboam's harsh answer led to the division of the kingdom
Describe Hezekiah's prayer when Jerusalem was threatened by Assyria and how God answered it
Compare the Northern Kingdom of Israel and the Southern Kingdom of Judah in their capitals, royal lines, and places of worship
Trace how Solomon's many wives and wealth turned his heart from the LORD in light of the law for kings
Classify kings such as Hezekiah, Josiah, Ahab, and Manasseh using the narrator's verdict of doing right or evil in the sight of the LORD
Analyze the ministries of Elijah and Elisha as prophets who confronted kings and performed signs that called Israel back to the covenant
Explain what God's appearance to Elijah at Horeb in the low whisper teaches about God's preservation of a faithful remnant
Connect Josiah's reforms to the finding of the Book of the Law in the Temple
Identify the pattern of prophecy and fulfillment in Kings using the prophecy against Bethel's altar and its fulfillment under Josiah
Explain the sin of Jeroboam's golden calves as a violation of the second commandment and trace its effect on later northern kings
Analyze the account of Naboth's vineyard to show how Ahab and Jezebel abused royal power against God's law
Construct a synchronized timeline of the kings of Israel and Judah using the regnal formulas of Kings alongside Assyrian and Babylonian history
Explain how Kings shows God keeping his promise to David through the preserved line of Judah and the release of Jehoiachin
Evaluate the role of the prophet in relation to the king in Kings using Nathan, Elijah, Micaiah, and Isaiah
Defend the Reformed reading of the fall of Samaria and Jerusalem as God's just judgment under the covenant curses of Deuteronomy
Produce a study of the contest between the LORD and Baal across Kings showing why the narrative condemns idolatry
Explain how the New Testament presents Jesus as greater than Solomon and links John the Baptist to Elijah

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Solomon, Elijah, division, Carmel, north versus south comparison, good and bad kings, Elijah and Elisha, Josiah, Jeroboam's calves, timeline, prophet and king, justice of exile, Yahweh versus Baal). Replaced the vague grade 3 idol observation with the narrator's evaluation formula at grade 6 and merged the fall of Samaria and Jerusalem into the covenant curse objective. Added missing content: God's provision for Elijah, Naaman, Hezekiah's prayer, Solomon's turning against the law for kings, Horeb and the remnant, prophecy and fulfillment, Naboth's vineyard, the Davidic promise and Jehoiachin's release, and New Testament connections to Christ and John the Baptist. Added verse-level scripture and confession anchors where they state the doctrine.
